message.content:
Civil law, also known as civil jurisprudence or civil law system, is a legal framework that governs non-criminal disputes between private parties. Its components can be broadly categorized into several key areas: | Component | Description | |-----------|-------------| | **Legal Sources** | • **Statutes & Codes** – Written laws enacted by legislatures (e.g., Civil Code, Commercial Code).
• **Case Law / Judicial Precedent** – Decisions from courts that interpret statutes and establish common law principles.
• **Customary Law** – Long‑standing practices recognized as binding in certain jurisdictions. | | **Legal Subjects** | • **Persons** – Natural persons, legal entities (companies, NGOs), and sometimes quasi‑persons (e.g., corporations).
• **Property** – Real property (land, buildings) and personal property (movable goods, intellectual property). | | **Legal Relationships** | • **Contracts** – Agreements that create obligations and rights.
• **Torts** – Wrongful acts causing harm or loss.
• **Family Law** – Marriage, divorce, child custody, adoption.
• **Inheritance & Succession** – Distribution of assets after death. | | **Legal Procedures** | • **Jurisdiction** – Determining which court has authority over a case.
• **Pleadings & Evidence** – Filing claims, defenses, and presenting evidence.
• **Trial & Judgment** – Conducting hearings, rendering decisions, and issuing orders. | | **Legal Remedies** | • **Damages** – Monetary compensation for loss or injury.
• **Specific Performance** – Court order requiring a party to fulfill contractual obligations.
• **Injunctions** – Orders preventing or mandating actions.
• **Restitution** – Returning property or value to the rightful owner. | | **Legal Institutions** | • **Courts** – Trial courts, appellate courts, specialized courts (family, commercial).
• **Regulatory Bodies** – Agencies overseeing specific sectors (e.g., consumer protection, securities).
• **Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR)** – Mediation, arbitration, conciliation mechanisms. | | **Legal Principles** | • **Good Faith & Fair Dealing** – Parties must act honestly and fairly.
• **Equitable Remedies** – Courts may grant relief beyond strict legal rules.
• **Presumption of Innocence** – In criminal law; in civil law, the burden of proof lies with the plaintiff. | | **Legal Documentation** | • **Contracts & Agreements** – Written or oral agreements.
• **Deeds & Titles** – Documents proving ownership of property.
• **Court Filings** – Pleadings, motions, affidavits. | These components interact to form a comprehensive system that addresses disputes, protects rights, and ensures orderly conduct in society. The exact structure and emphasis can vary by jurisdiction, but most civil law systems share these foundational elements.
